title: Safety thresholds for LLM behavioral drift: canary notes
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational working note for defining and testing safety thresholds tied specifically to behavioral drift signals during canary and A/B exposures of LLM-backed features. Goal is pragmatic: define a minimal, automatable threshold set that can (a) surface regressions in model behavior we care about, (b) be evaluated automatically in the console during progressive rollouts, and (c) map to deterministic gating/rollback actions.

Context and motivation:
- We’ve been shipping LLM changes more frequently; functional metrics (latency, token cost, error rates) are covered by existing rollout tooling but behavioral regressions (toxicity, hallucinations, identity bias, factuality drop) are harder to quantify quickly.
- Need a light-weight, standardized set of signals that product and SRE can agree on for canary slices, separate from long-form eval suites.
- This doc focuses on canary/AB exposures (0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) where we need fast, low-latency detection and clear human escalation paths.

Definitions (quick):
- Behavioral drift: measurable change in distribution of output-level safety/quality metrics vs baseline model/version.
- Canary slice: small subset of traffic used for early detection. Usually defined by user cohort (internal users, new users in region X), or randomized microcohort.
- Signal window: rolling 30m for immediate gating, 6h for trend confirmation, 72h for degradation confirmation.

Primary signals to compute in realtime (prioritized):
1) Safety toxicity score (per-response): aggregate of toxicity classifiers (model + external) normalized 0-1.
   - Metric: pct of responses > 0.7 toxicity in slice.
   - Baseline comparator: same slice baseline model (pinned) over last 7 days.
2) Hallucination proxy (factuality classifier + citation-absence rate):
   - Metric: pct of answers flagged by fact-checker as low-confidence (score < 0.4) + pct of responses with zero citations/structured references where previously expected.
3) Response-repetition/looping rate:
   - Metric: pct of sessions with repeated identical completions (>3 repeats in thread).
4) Harmful-content triggers (rule-based): explicit match counts for high-confidence patterns (self-harm, illegal instructions).
5) User escalation rate (downstream): percentage of canary users opening a support ticket or triggering a safety incident flag within 24h of interaction.

Threshold design principles:
- Prefer relative thresholds (x% increase over baseline) for signals sensitive to user and slice composition; use absolute thresholds for high-confidence harm signals.
- Two-tier thresholds: soft-alert (inform stakeholders, pause ramp) and hard-trigger (automatic rollback to fallback model).
- Avoid hypersensitivity on low-volume slices: require minimum n = 200 responses in window for soft, n = 1000 for hard.

Suggested threshold matrix (starting point; tune per-product):
- Toxicity: soft = 2× baseline OR absolute > 1.5% responses >0.7; hard = 4× baseline OR absolute > 3.0% (window 30m, min n=200).
- Hallucination-proxy: soft = 1.8× baseline OR +3 p.p. absolute; hard = 3× baseline OR +6 p.p. (6h window, min n=300).
- Repetition: soft = +5 p.p. absolute vs baseline; hard = +12 p.p. (30m window).
- Harmful rule matches: soft = any single high-confidence match (notify); hard = >=3 distinct high-confidence matches in 30m -> immediate rollback.
- User escalation: soft = 2× baseline; hard = 4× baseline or >=5 escalations in 1h.

Operational flow (canary stage):
- When soft threshold fires: automatically create an incident ticket in triage queue, notify the SRE/product rotation channel, mark canary as "paused ramp" in console. Human reviewer assigned within 30m.
- If signal resolves within 2h to below soft level -> document and resume planned ramp with a 1-step stall.
- If hard threshold fires: automated rollback to pinned fallback model; page oncall SRE + product lead. Mark traffic routing to fallback and start postmortem.

Human-in-the-loop review protocol:
- Triage checklist for reviewer (sticky in console): sample 50 random responses from canary slice (stratified by intent). Quick-label: toxic / hallucinated / poor-quality / ok. Prefer short manual labels; supplement with auto-classifier outputs.
- If manual review confirms majority of sampled responses problematic -> escalate to safety SME and keep rollback.
- If inconclusive -> expand sampling to 200 and re-check trends (6h window).

A/B experiments integration notes:
- A/B comparisons need paired-slice baselines. Always run the control and variant concurrently on randomized traffic to reduce selection bias.
- For low-frequency harmful events, use aggregate cumulative tests over larger windows (72h) but keep canary hard thresholds to protect users.
- Include a safety-focused QoS metric in A/B result table: composite score = weighted toxic_p + hallucination_p + harm_rule_count (weights to be tuned by product).

Console & alerting requirements (implementable hooks):
- Real-time rolling windows (30m, 6h) surfaced per rollout slice.
- Composite "safety health" score (0–100) with traffic-weighted baseline comparison.
- Automatic incident creation with pre-filled context: model version, slice definition, sample payloads, classifier outputs, and last 3 commits that touched model/serving.
- Easy rollback button that both flips routing and pins older model in the catalog for a configurable cool-down period.

Open questions / unknowns (to resolve in follow-ups):
- Exact classifier stacks: how many external vs in-house classifiers do we trust for operational gating? (action: Samir to prototype combined ensemble by 2026-01-10).
- Minimum sample sizes per product slice vary widely; need product-specific tuning guidelines (action: product leads provide slice volume estimates).
- How to avoid attacker-driven poisoning of canaries (malicious traffic that intentionally triggers safety signals)? Consider internal-only canaries or rate-limited ramping.

Short-term action items (next 4 sprints):
- S1: Implement toxicity + harm-rule detectors into rollout metrics feed + console badge (owner: engineering-observability, PR referenced above).
- S2: Ship soft/hard alerting config UI (product-console-rollouts) and default thresholds for hosted chat and search endpoints.
- S3: Pilot the protocol on a low-risk feature (internal power users cohort) for 2 weeks and capture false-positive rate.
- S4: Draft operator playbook (one-pager) for reviewers with sample scripts and escalation contact list.

Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally conservative for the first pass. We expect to iterate thresholds by product based on signal fidelity and false positive noise. The aim is to buy time and reduce user harm while keeping ramping predictable and fast for high-quality model changes.

Appendix: quick checklist for rollout owners (copy into PR template)
- Have you chosen the canary slice(s) and recorded expected baseline metrics? (Y/N)
- Is the sample size expected to exceed soft threshold n within first 30m? (Y/N)
- Do the linked safety classifiers exist and are they versioned? (Y/N)
- Have you attached a rollback plan and pinned fallback model? (Y/N)
- Contacts assigned for 30m triage and 24h postmortem? (list)

End of working notes.

(Author: Lena Chen — product-console-rollouts)

Unresolved: please add product-specific baseline numbers and surface any historical incidents we can use to tune hard thresholds.
